newsitem.title: USA: Amerada Hess to focus on exploration.
newsitem.headline: Amerada Hess to focus on exploration.

text.p: Amerada Hess Corp expects exploration and production to be the vehicle to future growth and value, Chief Executive John Hess said Wednesday.
About "90 percent of the corporation's capital expenditures in the future will be dedicated to exploration and production," he told the annual meeting.
President Sam Laidlaw told shareholders "Our goal is to achieve both double digit returns and 500,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day net production by the year 2000."
The company expects production will total 350,000 per day this year, spokesman Carl Tursi said.
Asked how much growth would be needed for Hess exploration and production to have double digit returns, Tursi said only "considerable."
During the meeting, Hess noted the company's first quarter refining and marketing loss was due to FIFO -- first in first out -- accounting for the company's refinery inventories.
Asked after the meeting if the company were going to change to LIFO -- last in first out -- accounting, he said "LIFO is a tax issue."
He indicated the change would be made "when it's right for taxes," adding that is "not now with (the company's tax) loss in the Virgin Islands" where it operates a 125,000 barrel per day refinery.
Hess told shareholders "Our objective is to become the leading independent oil company in each of our businesses.
"Our goal is to be in the top one third of oil companies in terms of capital employed."
